pages.text: The network adds up the power used by every consumer and compares it with the power generated.

If consumption is $(item)higher$() than generation, the whole network is marked $(item)Not Enough Power$(). Every machine on it stops at once: motors stop turning, lamps go dark, the polarizer stops charging. It is not only the last machine you placed that fails.$(br2)$(l)How to fix it$()
$(li)Add generators, or spin the ones you have faster.$(li)Remove or switch off consumers. When a block is removed, the network is checked again right away.
$(li)Split the factory into separate networks with switches, diodes or transformers (see $(item)Network Control$()), so one hungry machine cannot stall everything.

Hold a $(item)multimeter$() and look at any block of the network. The red line $(item)Not Enough Power$() tells you the network is short. Sneak while looking to see the network's total $(item)generation$() and $(item)consumption$() side by side.
